R0801.summary: Branislav Žarković is a Full Professor in Finance and Banking at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, with demonstrated expertise in credit risk, SME finance, and bank risk practice. His work centers on credit scoring for thin-file and micro-enterprise borrowers, alternative data and open banking in underwriting, explainable machine learning for lending, and the regulatory implications of AI and credit models. He also has prior industry experience as a head of risk at a regional bank, which informs his applied research profile.

expertise.topic: Credit scoring for thin-file borrowers and micro-enterprises
SME finance and credit access analysis
Alternative data and open banking in lending
Explainable and interpretable credit risk models
Regulatory and capital implications of machine learning credit models

R0919.summary: Martina Lačoková is a Senior Research Associate in computing and control engineering whose demonstrated work centers on testing and verification for embedded, automotive, and industrial control software, especially CAN-based systems and multi-supplier integration.

expertise.topic: Combinatorial interaction testing and constrained covering arrays
CAN/CAN FD integration testing and multi-supplier embedded systems
Formal methods, interface contracts, and compositional verification
Runtime verification and monitoring for embedded control software

R0995.summary: Veljko Pantelić (R0995) is an Assistant Professor in Computing and Control Engineering with a research profile centered on software engineering for industrial automation, especially model-driven engineering and domain-specific language tooling for IEC 61131-3 PLC software. His work also covers software product lines, code generation, variability management, safety-aware automation workflows, and related empirical evaluation and benchmarking.

Domain-specific language design and implementation for industrial control systems
Safety-aware automation software and traceability in certified PLC workflows

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on plain-language explanations for automated SME credit decisions at Kredo Fintech
proposal.problem: Kredo Fintech needs a compliant explanation format for automated credit decisions that can be generated at decision time, stored with the decision record, and shown in the borrower portal in Serbian and Macedonian. The current gradient-boosted model performs well, but the existing technical SHAP-based summary is not understandable enough for borrowers and does not satisfy the company’s compliance expectations. The practical problem is to turn model drivers into short, accurate, borrower-facing explanations that remain faithful to the decision and can be deployed in production within about six months.
research_questions: How can feature attributions from Kredo Fintech’s current gradient-boosted model be transformed into plain-language explanations that borrowers understand and can challenge?
Can an explanation template achieve a measurable improvement in borrower comprehension while preserving fidelity to the automated decision and meeting Kredo Fintech’s compliance requirements?
What Serbian and Macedonian explanation wording and storage format can be integrated into decision-time underwriting without slowing the existing production workflow beyond agreed limits?

plan.work: Map the current decision workflow, review the existing SHAP-based internal summary, define the explanation taxonomy, and design Serbian borrower-facing templates. Build a prototype that generates explanations at decision time and stores them with the decision record. Prepare a transfer check for Kredo Fintech’s Python, dbt, Snowflake, Airflow, scikit-learn, PostgreSQL, REST API and Docker environment.
plan.result: A tested prototype explanation module, a Serbian wording set, and a storage specification that can be reviewed by compliance and engineering.
plan.pass_if: The prototype produces an explanation for at least 95% of test decisions, each explanation is under 120 words, and Kredo Fintech confirms that it can be executed in their own stack without manual rewriting.

plan.work: Run iterative user testing with borrower-facing samples and internal review with compliance. Refine wording for clarity, challengeability, and fidelity. Add Macedonian rendering and confirm that both languages preserve the same decision logic and legal meaning.
plan.result: A validated bilingual explanation format ready for controlled production use.
plan.pass_if: At least 70% of test participants correctly identify the main reason for a sample decision, and compliance signs off that the output meets the intended plain-language standard for Serbian and Macedonian.

plan.work: Monitor explanation stability in production, assess error cases, and study whether the explanations affect borrower questions, complaints, or manual reviews. Write the doctoral thesis and produce publishable results on explanation quality for thin-file and micro-business lending.
plan.result: A production-tested explanation method, thesis, and research outputs on explainability in SME credit scoring.
plan.pass_if: The deployed format remains available for all automated decisions in the agreed scope, with documented exception handling for edge cases, and the final thesis demonstrates fidelity, usability, and operational fit on Kredo Fintech’s data.

proposal.company_brings: Kredo Fintech brings a regulated lending setting, its current automated underwriting flow, transaction data, tax filings, sector benchmarks, the existing gradient-boosted scoring model, the current SHAP-based internal summary, borrower portal integration needs, and access to its data team of five for implementation work within its production constraints.
proposal.faculty_brings: Branislav Žarković brings expertise in credit scoring for thin-file borrowers, alternative data, explainable credit risk models, and regulatory implications of machine learning credit models, supported by his Faculty of Economics in Subotica role and his prior banking risk experience.
proposal.why_this_pair: This pair fits because Kredo Fintech needs a production-ready explanation layer for SME lending, while Branislav Žarković has published directly on explainability, alternative data, thin-file scoring, and the regulatory side of credit models. His industry background in bank risk also matches the operational and compliance nature of the problem.
proposal.novelty: The closest prior work is SYN-PUB-08747, which studies explaining credit decisions to supervisors: a case study, and SYN-PUB-08751, which addresses explainability requirements under the EU AI Act. This project goes beyond those papers by turning explanation research into a live borrower-facing workflow for a Serbian fintech lender, with decision-time generation, bilingual Serbian-Macedonian delivery, storage alongside the decision record, and production validation in Kredo Fintech’s own underwriting stack.
proposal.data_status: The records state that Kredo Fintech already uses transaction data, tax filings, sector benchmarks, and a gradient-boosted ensemble scoring model, and that it has experimented with SHAP values and a short internal technical summary. The records do not state that borrower comprehension test data, complaint data, or Macedonian explanation text already exist, so those would need to be collected during the project.
proposal.first_step: Next month, agree the explanation output format, define a sample set of recent decisions for testing, and run a transfer check from the research prototype to Kredo Fintech’s Python, Snowflake, PostgreSQL and REST-based production environment.
proposal.to_agree: Funding for the doctoral candidate and supervision time; which side covers engineering time for implementation and testing; IP ownership and licensing for new explanation templates, software, and any background IP; publication review delay and confidentiality terms; access to decision records, SHAP outputs, borrower portal logs, and any user-testing participants; and the exact compliance sign-off process before any live deployment.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on contract-driven integration testing for multi-supplier CAN stacks at DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.
proposal.problem: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. reports that its LDRA branch coverage is already 87–89%, yet CAN communication faults still appear after delivery, especially at boundaries between components from different suppliers. research_questions: Can interface contracts extracted from ARXML and COM configurations be turned into measurable fault-targeting tests that reveal cross-supplier CAN interaction bugs earlier than current practice?
Do contract-directed test suites find more boundary faults than branch-coverage-driven integration tests at the same or lower test effort on DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. projects?
Which contract properties and generation constraints give the best trade-off between fault detection, execution time, and maintainability in AUTOSAR Classic CAN integration testing?

plan.work: Map the company’s current CAN integration workflow, define the contract model for ARXML/COM boundary assumptions, and build a prototype generator that produces test scenarios in the company’s own CANoe-based environment. Validate that generated tests transfer to DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.’s toolchain before any result is claimed.
plan.result: A working prototype that derives boundary-focused test scenarios from project descriptions and runs them in the company environment on at least one real integration case.
plan.pass_if: At least one company project yields a generated test set that executes in CANoe and exposes at least one previously undetected boundary case or reproduces a known supplier-interface fault with a smaller or equally sized suite than the current manually written integration tests.

plan.work: Extend the generator to handle multiple supplier interface patterns, add ranking/prioritization for high-risk contracts, and compare generated suites against existing branch-coverage-oriented tests on several historical or ongoing projects.
plan.result: An evaluated method for contract-directed integration testing with repeatable metrics for fault detection, effort, and coverage.
plan.pass_if: On at least two projects, the contract-directed suite finds more boundary faults per executed test case than the company’s current integration tests, or matches their fault yield with at least 20% fewer executed test cases.

plan.work: Harden the method into a usable workflow for DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o., document adoption guidelines, and assess whether it can be embedded in the company’s normal pre-delivery test planning with acceptable engineering overhead.
plan.result: A thesis-grade industrial method plus a practical workflow for recurring use on AUTOSAR Classic projects.
plan.pass_if: The company can apply the workflow to a new project without researcher intervention for the core generation step, and the team judges that the method fits within the stated phase-one budget envelope and normal project cadence.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on incremental PLC variability management for safer patching across 38 TIA Portal codebases
proposal.problem: AutomVoj a.d. has 38 active PLC codebases in TIA Portal, each written in ladder logic and diverged over time. A safety-related patch currently requires three engineers for two full weeks, and two of the 38 sites did not accept the standard fix cleanly in the last patch round. The practical problem is to introduce modular reuse and structured change management without rewriting all installations at once, while keeping the approach maintainable by a small team under daily project pressure.
research_questions: Can a family-level variability model capture the common and customer-specific parts of AutomVoj a.d.'s 38 ladder-logic codebases well enough to support safe patch propagation?

Can incremental code generation or transformation reduce the effort of applying a safety patch from three engineers for two full weeks to a repeatable update workflow that can be executed and verified on a subset of installations first?
Can the proposed method preserve compatibility with AutomVoj a.d.'s TIA Portal and Siemens S7-based toolchain while providing traceable impact analysis for safety-related changes?

plan.work: Elicit a representative subset of the 38 codebases with Dragan Ilić and one senior automation engineer, identify common ladder-logic patterns, and define a variability model and patch taxonomy for recurring safety changes. Build a prototype extraction and comparison workflow in the researcher's modeling toolchain, then check transfer to AutomVoj a.d.'s TIA Portal environment.
plan.result: A validated variability model for the first subset and a prototype workflow that can classify and localize a safety patch across the selected codebases.
plan.pass_if: At least 8 codebases are mapped into the family model, and the prototype localizes the target safety patch sites with no more than 1 manual correction per codebase in the pilot set.

plan.work: Develop incremental transformation or regeneration support so that a change in the family model produces candidate updates for customer-specific codebases instead of full rewrites. Validate the workflow on additional installations using historical patch cases and compare the resulting diffs with the current manual process.
plan.result: A repeatable incremental update pipeline with measurable reduction in manual edit effort for safety patches.
plan.pass_if: On at least 12 codebases, the generated update reduces manual editing time by at least 50 percent relative to the current baseline and preserves the intended safety behavior in offline tests.

plan.work: Extend the approach to the full set of 38 active codebases, add traceability for patch provenance and customer-specific deviations, and harden the method for routine use by AutomVoj a.d. engineers. plan.pass_if: The method supports all 38 codebases, and at least 30 of them can receive the target patch through the workflow with less than one engineer-day of manual adaptation each.

plan.work: Consolidate the results into doctoral outputs, document limitations, and package guidelines for future extensions to new conveyor projects. Finalize the industrial PhD thesis and the handover package for continued company use.

plan.pass_if: A defensible thesis is completed, and AutomVoj a.d. confirms that the documented workflow can be maintained by its existing automation staff without external support for one additional patch cycle.
